title: Choose the About page structure
question: Your steer, Datasheet + Index, leads this hand; the roll dealt three fresh structures beside it. Lock one, steer again, or re-roll.

options.label: Datasheet + Index
options.lineage: The Datasheet's front page over The Index's skills section
options.thesis: Bio and a ruled facts table share the first viewport; the skills index with project links follows across the grid.
options.viewport: Bio in a reading column on the left; Education, Experience, Languages and base in a ruled table on the right; the skills index opens at the fold.
options.risk: The facts table ends well before the bio does, so the right half sits empty for a stretch on wide screens.

options.label: Facing Pages
options.lineage: A book's open spread: text on the left page, index on the right
options.thesis: The bio and the skills index sit side by side as one spread, with education, experience and languages in a strip beneath.
options.viewport: Bio on the left half; the six skill groups in two index columns on the right half, references in cobalt.
options.risk: Two dense halves compete for the eye, and on phones the spread collapses into a plain stack.

options.label: Chapters
options.lineage: Home's label-and-body sections, one per bio paragraph
options.thesis: Each bio paragraph becomes its own section carrying the facts it mentions: education with study, skills with the homelab, languages with the last.
options.viewport: Title, then the first section: its label on the left, paragraph one with education and experience set beneath it.
options.risk: The section labels are new copy, and the skill groups end up split across three sections.

options.label: Contents Rail
options.lineage: A manual's side contents, held as a sticky rail
options.thesis: A sticky contents rail in the label column tracks the five sections on the right, the current one marked by the cobalt Now line.
options.viewport: Contents list in the label column with Bio marked; the bio opens in the body column beside it.
options.risk: Five sections on one page hardly need contents, and marking the current one takes client JavaScript.
